article.headline: Aaron Judge's Calf Injury Clouds Yankees' Wild Card Opener Against Red Sox Tonight

research.facts:
Aaron Judge Calf Injury — Yankees Without Their Captain
**Sources searched:** athlonsports.com, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, USNews, ESPN, mlb.com, yardbarker.com
**Verified Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Judge has been dealing with right calf strain (soleus muscle)
- Last played September 16
- Boone said Monday: Yankees are "planning on him not being a part of" Wild Card series vs. Red Sox, though not ruling it out
- Judge hoped to take batting practice Monday to test the calf
- Judge played only 66 games in 2026 — lowest career total excluding shortened 2020 and 2016 debut
- Judge also dealt with right rib stress fracture earlier in 2026 season
- Yankees vs Red Sox Wild Card Game 1 tonight 8 PM ET (NBC/Peacock)
- Yankees are the No. 4 AL seed; Red Sox are the No. 5 AL seed
**Sources:**

stories.title: White Sox: Three Straight 100-Loss Seasons to the Playoffs

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
The Chicago White Sox had 324 losses in 3 years.

Their 2024 record of 121 losses is the worst in MLB history.

Their Opening Day 2026 playoff odds: 1.1%.

Tonight they play in the postseason at Houston. First in MLB history after 3 straight 100-loss seasons. ⚾

#WhiteSox

article.headline: From 121 Losses to October Baseball: The White Sox's Impossible Turnaround

research.facts:
White Sox — Three 100-Loss Seasons to Playoffs
**Sources searched:** ESPN, mlb.com, newstimes.com, beisbol.love, Daily Caller
**Verified Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- White Sox finished 84-78 in 2026
- Had three consecutive 100+ loss seasons before 2026 (2023, 2024, 2025)
- 2024 record: 121 losses — MLB record for most losses in a 162-game season
- 324 total losses over 3 seasons (2023-2025)
- Opening Day 2026 playoff odds: 1.1%
- Clinched playoff berth on September 24 with 9-1 win over Kansas City Royals
- First team in MLB history to reach playoffs after three straight 100-loss seasons
- Both Chicago teams (Cubs and White Sox) reached postseason — fourth time both Chicago teams in playoffs (1906, 2008, 2020, 2026)
- White Sox as No. 6 AL seed, play at No. 3 Astros tonight 5 PM ET
**Sources:**
- ESPN: "White Sox clinch playoff berth after three straight 100-loss seasons"
- mlb.com: "How the White Sox went from MLB's worst 162-game record to playoffs in just 2 years"
- Daily Caller: "White Sox Clinch Playoffs After 121-Loss Season"
- beisbol.love: "White Sox Clinch Playoffs After 121-Loss Season"

stories.title: Astros 81-81 — First Sub-.500 Division Champion in MLB History Opens Postseason Tonight

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
In 162 years of MLB history, no division champion had ever finished at .500 or below.

The 2026 Houston Astros finished 81-81 and won the AL West.

They host the White Sox tonight at 5 PM ET.

Baseball, man. 🤷 #Astros

article.headline: The 2026 Astros Made History With an 81-81 Record. Now They Host the Postseason.

research.facts:
Astros 81-81 — First Sub-.500 Division Champion
**Sources searched:** mlb.com, fox26houston.com, houstonpublicmedia.org, houstonchronicle.com, Yahoo Sports
**Verified Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Astros finished 81-81 in 2026
- Won AL West title on final day of regular season (Sunday, Sept 28)
- Beat A's 9-0 on final day
- First division champion in MLB history to finish with .500 or worse record (in 162-game era)
- One game ahead of Texas Rangers (80-82) in AL West
- Would have clinched even with a loss because Texas lost 6-4 to Minnesota
- Fifth AL West title in six years for Houston
- Ninth postseason trip in 10 years for Astros
- No team in AL West finished with a winning record in 2026
- Astros are No. 3 AL seed, host No. 6 White Sox tonight 5 PM ET
**Sources:**
- mlb.com: "Astros clinch 2026 AL West title"
- fox26houston.com: "Astros win AL West with 81-81 record, worst for first-place team"
- Yahoo Sports: "Astros take AL West to become first division champ without winning record in MLB history"
- houstonpublicmedia.org: "Houston Astros rebound from 11 games under .500 and win AL West"
